newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's Lee confident HongKong will succeed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's Lee confident HongKong will succeed.

text.p: Singapore elder statesman Lee Kuan Yew said he was confident HongKong would succeed under the leadership of its chief executive designate Tung Chee-hwa, state television reported on Sunday.
Senior Minister Lee said in an interview with a China-based magazine he firmly believed Singapore would continue to invest in HongKong, a sign of confidence in its future leader.
Tung has reassured world leaders that the territory's prosperous economic climate would remain unchanged after China takes over in July.
But Lee said that Tung would need time to sort out some of the problems left by Governor Chris Patten, the 28th and last governor of Hong Kong.
He criticised Patten for not making better use of his five years in office to prepare HongKong for its handover to China.
The territory, a British colony for more than 150 years, reverts to China at midnight on June 30 this year.
Lee, prime minister of Singapore from 1959 to 1990 and who continues to be outspoken on political and trade issues, has been a strong advocate for China's inclusion in the world economy.
His recent remarks, however, carried in an affidavit for a libel suit against an opposition leader, has embroiled Singapore in a diplomatic row with its northern neighbour.
He said the Malaysian state of Johor was "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings." REUTER jw
